Maya (docs): Heads-up — PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4523 shows query-param examples for /v1/search using `?include_snippets=true`, but a reviewer pointed out we have other examples using `?include_snippets=1`. Should we standardize and also document what values the server accepts?

Liam (backend): We use Go's strconv.ParseBool for those handlers. That accepts: `1`, `t`, `T`, `TRUE`, `true`, `True`, and the equivalents for false: `0`, `f`, `F`, `FALSE`, `false`, `False`. Important: `on`/`off` are NOT accepted. We should call that out explicitly.

Ellie (SDK): FYI JS/Go SDKs accept boolean types in the param objects and stringify them when making HTTP calls, so most apps won't care. The inconsistency is purely in our curl/inline-URL examples. My recommendation: use `true`/`false` in docs examples (more readable) and add a one-line note that server accepts `1`/`0` for legacy clients.

Maya (docs): Sounds good. I'll update the PR to: 1) change every query example to use `true`/`false`; 2) add a short "Accepted boolean tokens" bullet under the endpoint param table with the list Liam gave; 3) add a tiny SDK blurb: "SDKs accept booleans; examples show `true`/`false` in HTTP URLs." Planning to push shortly.

Liam (backend): One more thing — some endpoints are behind the legacy `legacyQueryCoercion` flag and have custom parsing. Might be worth a short callout in the endpoint notes if an endpoint still accepts non-standard tokens. Otherwise put the standard behavior in the global query-param style doc.

Ellie (SDK): I'll update the Go snippet in the SDK section to show how a server reads the query:

```
q := r.URL.Query().Get("preview")
ok, _ := strconv.ParseBool(q)
if ok { /* treat as true */ }
```

And add a JS example for callers: `fetch('/v1/search?preview=true')`.

Maya (docs): PR updated: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4523/files — changed examples + added accepted-tokens note. Can someone quick-review the wording? :)

deploy-bot: docs deploy preview built — https://deploy-preview-redwood-docs.example/status — Status: success :rocket:

Liam (backend): LGTM; tiny nit: instead of "case-insensitive" maybe phrase as "case-insensitive; accepted tokens: 1/0/t/f/true/false" so it's clear.

Ellie (SDK): Reviewed and approved. No SDK changes required beyond the small snippet update.

Maya (docs): Merging now. Thanks all :tada:
